correction.text: Egypt from Aswan to the Delta as Cliopatria's last New Kingdom shape draws it; unverified for the south

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -943..-838: the Delta (capitals Bubastis and Tanis) is certain; how far south Shoshenq I's authority reached is not on the pages opened (the 22nd Dynasty page names no land beyond its capitals; the 21st Dynasty page has the Theban priests ruling the south 'in all but name' until 943). The outline of Egypt is kept from Cliopatria's New Kingdom row, flagged unverified. The 23rd Dynasty page lists Harsiese A (880-860) among its Theban kings, so the south was perhaps already separate.

correction.text: the shape as drawn for -900..-838 only; from -837 Lower Egypt (new keyframe)

keyframe_review.note: -900..-801, 340,593 km2, bbox 23.5-31.7 N: the outline of Egypt. Holds for -900..-838 as unverified; from 837 the Twenty-third Dynasty is established in Upper Egypt (23rd Dynasty infobox 'Established: 837 BC'; Third Intermediate Period infobox 'Heracleopolis Magna c. 837-728 BC') and 'Shoshenq III of the Twenty-second Dynasty' controls 'Lower Egypt by 818 BC'. No area figure on the pages opened.

correction.text: Lower Egypt: the Delta around Bubastis and Tanis, from the Mediterranean to the Fayum edge (the Cliopatria shape drawn for the 23rd Dynasty)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, -837..-801: Lower Egypt. The dynasty's capitals (Bubastis, Tanis) are in the Delta, and 'Shoshenq III of the Twenty-second Dynasty controlling Lower Egypt by 818 BC'. This is the shape Cliopatria assigns to the Twenty-third Dynasty row (-800, 52,603 km2, bbox 28.9-31.5 N, Delta and Fayum edge): the two Cliopatria shapes of the 22nd and 23rd look swapped.

correction.text: use the Cliopatria shape drawn for the Twenty-third Dynasty: Lower Egypt around Bubastis and Tanis; Herakleopolis, where 'a Twenty-second Dynasty king named Shoshenq V was still in power around 766 BC', lies at its southern edge

keyframe_review.note: -800..-751, 166,128 km2, bbox 23.4-29.3 N, 28.2-32.6 E: Aswan to the Fayum, i.e. Upper and Middle Egypt, 600 km south of Bubastis and Tanis ('Capitals: Bubastis, Tanis'). The Twenty-third Dynasty page puts Thebes and Herakleopolis ('Capital: Thebes, Herakleopolis') and 'Upper Egypt including Thebes' under Osorkon III (798-769) in that dynasty. This shape fits the 23rd; the 22nd's land is the shape Cliopatria gave the 23rd. The infobox gives no area.

correction.text: use the Cliopatria shape drawn for the Twenty-third Dynasty for -750..-733; from 732 the Sais region goes to the 24th Dynasty and the remainder around Tanis shrinks to a small portion of Lower Egypt

keyframe_review.note: -750..-701, same 166,128 km2 Upper Egypt shape: wrong for the same reason. Lower Egypt (the 52,603 km2 shape Cliopatria drew for the 23rd) holds until 732; then Osorkon IV (730-716) 'only controlled a small portion of Lower Egypt' while Tefnakht holds Sais (c. 732-720) and Piye of Kush campaigns 728-716. The ledger carries the shrinkage.

region.text: the Delta around Bubastis and Tanis

ledger.note: 943: Shoshenq I founds the Twenty-second Dynasty. 'The dynasty was founded by Shoshenq I, who was of ancient Libyan origin'; infobox 'Established: 943 BC' (reign 943-922); capitals Bubastis and Tanis.

region.text: Middle and Upper Egypt, assumed from Cliopatria's outline

ledger.note: 943: Middle and Upper Egypt pass from the Theban priests' orbit to Shoshenq I (assumed). The 22nd Dynasty page is silent on Thebes and the south; Cliopatria draws one Egypt from Aswan to the Delta in these years, and the Theban line of the 23rd Dynasty page only appears with Harsiese A (880-860). Bridging, to be checked.

region.text: Upper Egypt with Thebes and Herakleopolis

ledger.note: 837: the Twenty-third Dynasty is established in the south. Infobox 'Established: 837 BC'; 'being more or less an offshoot of the Twenty-second Dynasty'; Third Intermediate Period infobox 'Heracleopolis Magna (c. 837-728 BC, Twenty-third Dynasty of Egypt)'.

region.text: Thebes and Upper Egypt, the field of the civil war

ledger.note: 826: civil war breaks out over Thebes. 'In Takelot II's fifteenth year a civil war broke out' (Takelot II, 840-815 BC on the page: year 15 = 826). The page gives no BC year for the war.

799: the civil war is settled. 'The conflict was only resolved in Year 39 of Shoshenq III' (reign 837-798 BC on the 22nd Dynasty page: year 39 = 799); 'Shoshenq III ... controlling Lower Egypt by 818 BC' and Osorkon III then 'went on to rule Upper Egypt including Thebes for 28 years' (798-769, 23rd Dynasty page).

c. 732: Tefnakht of Sais breaks away. 'Sais (c. 732-720 BC, Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt)' in the infobox; 'the combined forces of several native Egyptian rulers' including 'Tefnakht of Sais' faced Piye c. 732. Osorkon IV (730-716) 'only controlled a small portion of Lower Egypt' (22nd Dynasty page).

730: the court is at Tanis. 'The next ruler at Tanis after Shoshenq V was Osorkon IV' (730-716). [Reviewer me-03-b, 2026-10-18] Confidence 1: the 22nd Dynasty page says its rulers 'almost certainly governed from Tanis', their capital, throughout, and no page dates a move in 730; the Third Intermediate Period infobox has 'Bubastis (c. 943-716 BC)'. The 730 date is a bridge.

region.text: Lower Egypt, where Piye 'seized control ... around 727 BC'

ledger.note: 728: Piye of Kush campaigns in Egypt. The Victory Stela celebrates 'these campaigns between 728 and 716 BC'; the Third Intermediate Period page has Piye marching north 'around 732 BC'.
716: the last campaign year of the Victory Stela (728-716). Osorkon IV's reign ends 716 on the 22nd Dynasty page.

region.text: what remained of Lower Egypt around Tanis

ledger.note: 716: the Twenty-second Dynasty ends. Infobox 'Disestablished: 716 BC'; Osorkon IV 730-716. The Kush page: Piye 'seized control of Lower Egypt around 727 BC'; Kushite direct rule of the Delta is dated later in the Kush dossier.

wars.name: Theban civil war of Takelot II
wars.outcome: Settled in Year 39 of Shoshenq III; the Twenty-third Dynasty keeps Upper Egypt with Thebes (Osorkon III 798-769).
wars.note: The 23rd Dynasty page counts Takelot II among its own kings (840-815), the 22nd Dynasty table does not list him: the two pages classify the Thebes line differently.

wars.name: Piye's conquest of Egypt
wars.outcome: Kushite victory: the native rulers (Tefnakht of Sais, Osorkon IV and others) are defeated; the Twenty-fifth Dynasty follows.
wars.note: Kush page: 'between 728 and 716 BC'; Third Intermediate Period page: 'around 732 BC his successor, Piye, marched north and defeated' the native rulers.

certainty.note: No frontier of the Libyan-age kingdoms is described by the pages opened; the Delta/Upper Egypt line is approximate throughout.

notes:
Cliopatria rows: 'Twenty-second Dynasty of Egypt' (-800..-701) and the last shape of 'New Kingdom of Egypt' (-900..-801, reviewed here) are claimed by this dossier; the other New Kingdom shapes are in new-kingdom-of-egypt and twenty-first-dynasty-of-egypt (the validator warns about them: intended).
The two Cliopatria shapes of the 22nd and 23rd Dynasties look swapped: the 22nd row (166,128 km2, 23.4-29.3 N) is Upper and Middle Egypt, the 23rd row (61,633 km2 on shapes.csv, 52,603 km2 resolved, 28.9-31.5 N) is the Delta. The pages opened put the 22nd at Bubastis and Tanis (Lower Egypt) and the 23rd at Thebes and Herakleopolis (Upper Egypt). Both dossiers swap them. Cliopatria's single Seshat id for both is eg_thebes_libyan.
Pages disagree: the Third Intermediate Period page dates the 22nd Dynasty's foundation 945 BC (or 943), the dynasty page 943; the 23rd Dynasty page counts Harsiese A (880-860) and Takelot II (840-815) as 23rd Dynasty kings and ends the dynasty 728 in the infobox but names Ini (720-715) and Shabataka in 712; the 22nd Dynasty table lists Pedubast II (743-733) where the 23rd page's Tanite list has c. 730-725. The 22nd Dynasty page is thin: nothing on Shoshenq I's Levantine campaign (the Third Intermediate Period page does not date one either), on Thebes before 837, on Osorkon II or on the breakup; a gap-filler should open 'Shoshenq I', 'Osorkon II', 'Takelot II', 'Libyan period' and 'Twenty-fourth Dynasty of Egypt'.
Counterparts without dossiers: twenty-fourth-dynasty-of-egypt (Sais, c. 732-720), high-priests-of-amun-at-thebes (see the 21st Dynasty dossier). The ledger event 943 'gain Upper Egypt' is confidence 1: the page is silent on the south.
Gazetteer lacks Bubastis (Tell Basta, 30.57 N 31.51 E), Herakleopolis Magna, Leontopolis. No infobox area on any page opened; Cliopatria areas not comparable.
